paragraphs: I'm applying for the Analyst role on the Power & Utilities team in New York. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. The posting's point about data centers and AI driving new electricity demand is exactly why I want to cover this sector. Power and data center financing is the area I most want to build a career in, and your team's record as a lead arranger for utilities and renewable developers is a strong place to learn it.

The closest work I've done is an MBA project modeling a 6-project, 35.4 MW Illinois solar portfolio. I built project and portfolio models covering capital structure, DSCR, NPV and levered IRR under post-ITC scenarios, compared senior debt, sustainability-linked loan and green loan plus ABS structures, and recommended a phased green loan + ABS approach that reduced sponsor equity by $11.1M in the model and improved levered IRR from 8.58% to 9.79%. At Lenovo I spent two years building forecasts and scenario analyses that improved capital efficiency by 15%.

That maps to the modeling, credit work and presentation drafting the role describes. My project finance work so far has been coursework, so I'd be learning live execution on the job, but I bring careful Excel modeling, comfort with debt metrics, and real interest in how utilities and IPPs fund new generation. I'd welcome the chance to talk.

outreach: Hi [Name], I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli and I'm applying for the Power & Utilities Analyst role at MUFG. For an MBA project I modeled a 35.4 MW solar portfolio (DSCR, levered IRR, green loan + ABS structures), and at Lenovo I built forecasts that improved capital efficiency by 15%. I'd love to hear how the team is seeing data center power demand. Would you have 15 minutes for a quick chat?
